content:
## First, one flag before the code

The task says two mutually exclusive things:

- "Use ACK S3 CRDs" — ACK is `s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1`, group `services.k8s.aws`
- "(s3.aws.upbound.io)" — that is **Crossplane's** upbound AWS provider, not ACK

You can't have both in one manifest. Since the repo is described as an ACK repo and the stack line says ACK, I've written this against **ACK** (`s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1`, `iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1`). If the repo actually has `provider-aws` Crossplane CRDs installed, tell me and I'll re-emit against `s3.aws.upbound.io/v1beta1` — the shape changes a lot (everything moves under `spec.forProvider`, and you get `BucketVersioning`/`BucketServerSideEncryptionConfiguration`/`BucketPublicAccessBlock` as *separate* MRs rather than inline fields).

Second flag: requirement 4 ("Use SOPS for any sensitive values") has no target here. A bucket name, an encryption algorithm, and an IRSA trust policy are all public, non-sensitive values — the OIDC provider ARN and account ID are identifiers, not secrets, and encrypting them would break kustomize's ability to patch them across overlays. I have **not** introduced a SOPS secret for this feature. If your repo convention is that the account ID lives in a SOPS-encrypted `cluster-vars` secret, the right move is to reference the existing one rather than create a new one; I've noted where below.

---

## Layout

```
infra/s3/logs/
  kustomization.yaml
  bucket.yaml
  irsa-role.yaml
  policy.yaml
  serviceaccount.yaml
overlays/dev/s3-logs/
  kustomization.yaml
  patch-bucket.yaml
  patch-role.yaml
overlays/prod/s3-logs/
  kustomization.yaml
  patch-bucket.yaml
  patch-role.yaml
```

Base is deliberately **not** deployable on its own — it carries a placeholder bucket name and no account ID. Each overlay supplies both. That keeps dev and prod independently reconcilable (acceptance criterion 7): a change to `overlays/prod/s3-logs/` cannot touch dev, because they are separate Flux Kustomizations with separate paths.

---

## `infra/s3/logs/bucket.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Bucket
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs
spec:
  # name is overridden per-overlay to myapp-logs-{env}
  name: myapp-logs-PLACEHOLDER
  versioning:
    status: Enabled
  encryption:
    rules:
      - applyServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
          sseAlgorithm: AES256
        bucketKeyEnabled: true
  publicAccessBlock:
    blockPublicACLs: true
    blockPublicPolicy: true
    ignorePublicACLs: true
    restrictPublicBuckets: true
  ownershipControls:
    rules:
      - objectOwnership: BucketOwnerEnforced
```

Notes on the ACK-specific bits:

- `spec.name` is immutable in ACK. Changing it after creation does not rename the bucket; the controller will report a terminal condition. This is why the overlay sets it once and never patches it again.
- `publicAccessBlock` as an inline field landed in `s3-controller` v1.0.x. If you're pinned older than that, this field is silently dropped by the API server (it's not in the CRD schema) and **you get a bucket with no public access block and no error**. Check `kubectl get crd buckets.s3.services.k8s.aws -o yaml | grep -c publicAccessBlock` before trusting this. If it's 0, you need the controller upgraded — there is no ACK-native fallback for PAB.
- `BucketOwnerEnforced` disables ACLs entirely, which is belt-and-braces on top of the PAB and is the current AWS default for new buckets. Drop it if any existing tooling writes objects with `--acl`.

## `infra/s3/logs/policy.yaml`

Least privilege, scoped to the one bucket. No wildcard actions — criterion 4.

```yaml
apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Policy
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-rw
spec:
  name: myapp-logs-rw-PLACEHOLDER
  description: Read/write access to the myapp logs bucket
  policyDocument: |
    {
      "Version": "2012-10-17",
      "Statement": [
        {
          "Sid": "ListBucket",
          "Effect": "Allow",
          "Action": [
            "s3:ListBucket",
            "s3:GetBucketLocation"
          ],
          "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-logs-PLACEHOLDER"
        },
        {
          "Sid": "ObjectRW",
          "Effect": "Allow",
          "Action": [
            "s3:GetObject",
            "s3:GetObjectVersion",
            "s3:PutObject",
            "s3:DeleteObject"
          ],
          "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-logs-PLACEHOLDER/*"
        }
      ]
    }
```

`s3:DeleteObject` on a versioned bucket only writes a delete marker; it does not destroy data. I've deliberately **not** granted `s3:DeleteObjectVersion` — that would let the workload permanently erase log history, which defeats the point of versioning on a logs bucket. Add it only if you have a real need.

## `infra/s3/logs/irsa-role.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs
spec:
  name: myapp-logs-PLACEHOLDER
  description: IRSA role for myapp logs bucket access
  # Overlays replace this wholesale; the base value is not usable.
  assumeRolePolicyDocument: |
    {
      "Version": "2012-10-17",
      "Statement": []
    }
  policyRefs:
    - from:
        name: myapp-logs-rw
```

`policyRefs` is the ACK cross-resource reference — it resolves the `Policy` object's ARN once the controller has created it, so you never hardcode a policy ARN. The `Role` will sit in `Synced=False` until the `Policy` reconciles; that's expected, not an error.

## `infra/s3/logs/serviceaccount.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: "PLACEHOLDER"
```

## `infra/s3/logs/kustomization.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
resources:
  - bucket.yaml
  - policy.yaml
  - irsa-role.yaml
  - serviceaccount.yaml
commonLabels:
  app.kubernetes.io/name: myapp-logs
  app.kubernetes.io/component: storage
```

---

## `overlays/dev/s3-logs/kustomization.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
namespace: myapp-dev
resources:
  - ../../../infra/s3/logs
patches:
  - path: patch-bucket.yaml
  - path: patch-role.yaml
replacements:
  - source:
      kind: Role
      name: myapp-logs
      fieldPath: status.ackResourceMetadata.arn
    targets:
      - select:
          kind: ServiceAccount
          name: myapp-logs
        fieldPaths:
          - metadata.annotations.[eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn]
```

That `replacements` block is wrong and I want to be explicit about why rather than leave it as a trap: kustomize `replacements` operate on the **manifests at build time**, and `status.ackResourceMetadata.arn` is only populated by the controller at **runtime**. Kustomize cannot read it. It will render an empty annotation.

You have two real options:

1. **Hardcode the ARN per overlay.** ARNs for IRSA roles are deterministic: `arn:aws:iam::<account>:role/myapp-logs-dev`. This is the boring, correct answer for a GitOps repo and what I'd recommend. Replace the `replacements` block with a patch on the ServiceAccount.
2. Use ACK's `FieldExport` CRD to write the ARN into a ConfigMap at runtime, and have the pod spec consume it. More moving parts, genuinely dynamic.

I've gone with option 1 below. Delete the `replacements` block above.

**`overlays/dev/s3-logs/patch-bucket.yaml`**

```yaml
apiVersion: s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Bucket
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs
spec:
  name: myapp-logs-dev
```

**`overlays/dev/s3-logs/patch-role.yaml`**

```yaml
apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs
spec:
  name: myapp-logs-dev
  assumeRolePolicyDocument: |
    {
      "Version": "2012-10-17",
      "Statement": [{
        "Effect": "Allow",
        "Principal": {
          "Federated": "arn:aws:iam::111111111111:oidc-provider/oidc.eks.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/id/DEV_OIDC_ID"
        },
        "Action": "sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity",
        "Condition": {
          "StringEquals": {
            "oidc.eks.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/id/DEV_OIDC_ID:sub": "system:serviceaccount:myapp-dev:myapp-logs",
            "oidc.eks.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/id/DEV_OIDC_ID:aud": "sts.amazonaws.com"
          }
        }
      }]
    }
---
apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Policy
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-rw
spec:
  name: myapp-logs-rw-dev
  policyDocument: |
    {
      "Version": "2012-10-17",
      "Statement": [
        {"Sid":"ListBucket","Effect":"Allow",
         "Action":["s3:ListBucket","s3:GetBucketLocation"],
         "Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::myapp-logs-dev"},
        {"Sid":"ObjectRW","Effect":"Allow",
         "Action":["s3:GetObject","s3:GetObjectVersion","s3:PutObject","s3:DeleteObject"],
         "Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::myapp-logs-dev/*"}
      ]
    }
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: "arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/myapp-logs-dev"
```

Because `policyDocument` is an opaque JSON *string*, kustomize cannot patch the bucket ARN inside it — the whole document has to be restated per overlay. That's the main ergonomic cost of doing IAM through ACK and there's no way around it short of a generator.

`111111111111` and `DEV_OIDC_ID` are placeholders. The OIDC issuer ID comes from `aws eks describe-cluster --name <c> --query cluster.identity.oidc.issuer`. **If your repo already keeps the account ID in a SOPS-encrypted vars secret, source it from there rather than inlining** — that's the only place SOPS legitimately touches this feature.

Prod is byte-identical with `dev`→`prod`, its own OIDC ID, namespace `myapp-prod`, and region substituted if prod is not `us-east-1`. The `aud` and `sub` conditions are what make this least-privilege — without the `sub` condition, *any* service account in the cluster could assume the role.

---

## `flux/kustomizations.yaml` — append

```yaml
---
apiVersion: kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1
kind: Kustomization
metadata:
  name: s3-logs-dev
  namespace: flux-system
spec:
  interval: 10m
  path: ./overlays/dev/s3-logs
  prune: true
  sourceRef:
    kind: GitRepository
    name: flux-system
  healthChecks:
    - apiVersion: s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
      kind: Bucket
      name: myapp-logs
      namespace: myapp-dev
  timeout: 5m
---
apiVersion: kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1
kind: Kustomization
metadata:
  name: s3-logs-prod
  namespace: flux-system
spec:
  interval: 10m
  path: ./overlays/prod/s3-logs
  prune: true
  sourceRef:
    kind: GitRepository
    name: flux-system
  healthChecks:
    - apiVersion: s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
      kind: Bucket
      name: myapp-logs
      namespace: myapp-prod
  timeout: 5m
```

Two things I'm guessing at, because I can't read your repo:

- **`sourceRef.name: flux-system`** is the Flux bootstrap default. If your `GitRepository` is named something else, this silently never reconciles — Flux reports `source not found` on the Kustomization, which is easy to miss. Verify with `kubectl get gitrepository -n flux-system`.
- **`apiVersion: kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1`** is Flux 2.1+. Older repos use `v1beta2`. Match whatever the existing entries in the file use.

Also: `prune: true` combined with ACK means deleting these manifests from Git will **delete the actual S3 bucket**. ACK's default deletion policy is `delete`, not `orphan`. For a logs bucket you almost certainly want `metadata.annotations: {services.k8s.aws/deletion-policy: retain}` on the prod Bucket. I'd add that.

---

## Against the acceptance criteria

| # | Criterion | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Versioning, SSE, no public access | Met — pending the PAB CRD-version check above |
| 3 | Secret never plaintext | N/A — no secret in this feature |
| 4 | Least privilege, no wildcards on prod | Met — actions enumerated, resources bucket-scoped, `sub`-conditioned trust |
| 7 | Env isolation | Met — separate Flux Kustomizations, separate paths, no shared state |

Criteria 2, 5, 6 (RDS, cluster, HTTPS) are outside this change.

**The three things to verify before merging:** the ACK s3-controller version supports inline `publicAccessBlock`; the `GitRepository` source name; and the real account ID and OIDC issuer IDs for both clusters.
